description: A violet stone with one lidded, slit-pupilled eye that follows the room. Gloompard has four. Its stone has one.
lore: The argument at the black-wood fires is the count. Four, say the people who have met it lately, and they are not wrong. Two, say the oldest heads, who learned it before those people were dead. Six, says a man on the north side who is believed about most other things. It never settles, because everyone who has ever counted was in the dark and frightened at the time.

Put the stones out on a bench and the argument does not end, it changes shape. Every one of them has one eye. Not a mark resembling an eye — an eye, lidded, slit through the middle, open, and tracking the room. Whatever [[monsters/shadow_panther|the animal]] has been given out there, what went all the way down was a single one. A drawing is somebody's bad evening. A hundred stones in a row are a count.

[[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] learned it with two, and gets told at the fire, kindly, that he has it muddled. He puts his stone on the table when that happens. It does not prove his number and he knows it does not; it proves the number went on from outside, that the fire has been adding to it for centuries, and that whatever the table is correcting him about, it is not the animal. He likes the quiet that follows better than he would like being right, and company is what he came for.

What a buyer gets, once it is set, is the other half of the meeting: the blow that lands from behind because nothing turned to meet it, and the few seconds afterwards where the smoke has you and the field does not.
gm_notes: The strongest evidence record in the batch: the eye count is unsettleable by encounter and settled — differently — by a bench of stones. Agrees with the creature record (four now, two once, telling does the adding) without restating Jehanne's argument about whether to stop telling it. Wendell trades memory for company; here he spends being wrong to buy an audience.
